tldr: Turning an outreach business into around forty typed tools an agent can call was easy. Building the walls that make it safe was the real work.
what: Exposing a whole outreach and lead-generation motion as typed tools an agent operates in production: campaigns, ads, email, SMS, WhatsApp, calls, social posts, opt-out checks, prospects, and conversations. Each tool has a defined shape for input and output.
why: Types only catch malformed calls. A perfectly typed send email is still a real message to a real person, possibly one who begged you to stop. The hard part is stopping well-formed calls from doing harm.
how: A compliance check in every send path that fails closed. Each API key bound to one tenant, with the tenant ID inside every query, so cross-tenant access cannot even be expressed. Ad accounts run server-side on a hidden token, with object IDs verified first. Ads are always created paused, so spending is a separate, deliberate act.
takeaway: The tools let the agent act. The walls, which never show up in the tool list, are what let you go to sleep while it works.
